solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In rapid succession — like a threatened rifleman's orders?

definitions.meaning: describes things happening one after another at speed
a rifleman under threat would be told to hurry and shoot, two commands in one breath

explanation.definitionFit: Rapid-fire questions or remarks come one after another without pause, and the military commands split into two words say the same.

clue.text: Drunk removing coat showing tuft of hair

indicators.note: taking off a coat strips the outer layer, so the word's first and last letters go

parts.note: squiffy is British slang for slightly drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk takes off his coat to reveal an odd hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: SQUIFFY is informal British for tipsy; 'removing coat' peels off S and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiff is a lock of hair brushed up and back from the forehead, a classic tuft.

clue.text: Lack of power by tail in collapsing after opening to innings

indicators.note: after places the anagram behind the single letter in the answer
the opening of a word is its first letter, taken here from innings
a collapsing batting order falls apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket team lacks batting power when its tail collapses after the openers go.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the tail is the weak lower batting order, so 'collapsing' fits the surface while signalling the rearrangement; 'after' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Inability is a lack of the power or means to do something; a synonym.

clue.text: Defile park? He's by ground with last of ruffians

indicators.note: ground means crushed or broken up, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here from ruffians

explanation.surface: A man mentions a park he walks past, ruffians loitering there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges PARK HES BY into KHYBERPAS; S, the 'last of ruffians', completes it. 'Defile' looks like a verb but is the noun, a narrow pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A defile is a narrow mountain pass, and the Khyber Pass between Afghanistan and Pakistan is the famous example.

clue.text: Awaiting within retail site?

definitions.meaning: something lying ahead, about to happen to someone

explanation.definitionFit: Something in store for you is coming soon, waiting for you; read literally the phrase places you inside a shop.

clue.text: Close to infuriation? Agreed after review

definitions.text: Close to infuriation? Agreed after review

indicators.note: a review goes over the letters again and sets them out anew, so they are rearranged
the close of a word is its final letter, taken here from infuriation

explanation.surface: Someone nearly furious is told everyone agreed once the matter was reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: N closes 'infuriation'; 'after review' rearranges it with AGREED to give the answer. The whole clue also hints at the meaning: past mere closeness to fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enraged is being infuriated, very angry, which the clue as a whole suggests.

clue.text: Revolutionary ship's competition on board?

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born Marxist revolutionary
SS, steamship, prefixes a ship's name

explanation.surface: A revolutionary vessel hosts a contest on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship's deck, but it is the board the game is played on.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a game played as a contest on a checkered board, hence a board competition.

clue.text: Some habit shown by cold and solemn chap

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
an owl is a byword for a solemn-looking person

explanation.surface: A habit worn by a cold, serious man, perhaps a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a monk's hood, a part of the habit he wears.

clue.text: Force out executive with decree

parts.note: ex is a dictionary abbreviation of executive
an act is a law or decree passed by a legislature

explanation.surface: A manager is forced out by official decree.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and obtain by force, as in exacting a payment or revenge.

clue.text: Irritable teen misbehaving in most of joint

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the shortened word
most of a word drops its last letter

parts.note: a splice is a joint made by joining rope ends or film

indicators.note: misbehaving letters are out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teenager acting up in a pub becomes bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a pub or a cannabis cigarette, but it is a woven join in rope; 'most of' trims it and 'misbehaving' scrambles the teenager.
explanation.definitionFit: Splenetic, from the spleen as seat of bad temper, means bad-tempered and spiteful.

clue.text: India with score that's 50 short? Another country

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so it is taken away

parts.note: a tally is a score or count
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: India's total falls fifty short, and another country wins the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's 50 short' removes L from TALLY to give TALY. 'Another' links back to India, also a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a country in southern Europe, one more nation alongside India.

clue.text: Figure associated with cooler delivery touched person

parts.note: screw is slang for a prison warder, and cooler is slang for prison
a bowler's delivery in cricket is a ball

explanation.surface: Someone linked to a refrigerated delivery van is a bit eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each delivery is a ball. 'touched' means slightly mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwball is an eccentric or crazy person, and touched means slightly unhinged.

clue.text: Food in audience ample? There's qualified agreement

indicators.note: heard by an audience, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: fare is food and drink
enough means sufficient or ample

explanation.surface: The theatregoers had plenty to eat, so there was grudging agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: FARE, food, said out loud gives FAIR. 'qualified' means limited, not certified.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying fair enough concedes a point reasonably but without full enthusiasm, a limited acceptance.

clue.text: Crop could be linked to this field's centre with endless colour

definitions.text: Crop could be linked to this

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter, here from field
something endless has lost its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a tone is a shade or colour

explanation.surface: A farmer's crop ties up with a field of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eton crop is a short 1920s women's haircut named after the English public school; 'Crop' looks agricultural.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eton crop was a boyishly short hairstyle, so the school's name pairs with this haircut word.

clue.text: Casual involvement shown by Irish for nothing in starting a business

indicators.note: one thing for another means swapping it in where the other was

parts.note: flotation is launching a company on the stock market
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Irish backers put money into a startup for nothing, a fling of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: IR replaces O in FLOTATION, the word 'in' placing it there. Flotation is selling a company's shares to the public for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: A flirtation is a light, non-committal romantic interest or a brief dabbling, a casual involvement.

clue.text: Government lies PM concocted? Get brief view

indicators.note: concocted means made up, so these letters are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: Voters get a glimpse of whether ministers' lies were invented by the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' rearranges LIES PM into LIMPSE; PM is the Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To glimpse is to see something briefly or partially; a synonym.

clue.text: Severe government decision about European line

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a ruling is an official decision

explanation.surface: A harsh government ruling on a European rail line.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruelling means exhausting and demanding, a harsh or severe ordeal.

clue.text: Shop and hotel found in good resort finally? It could be Turkish

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, is a food shop

indicators.note: found in places one piece inside the other
finally takes the last letter of the word, here from resort

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A shop and hotel in a good resort, maybe on the Turkish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkish delight is a gel sweet dusted with sugar; 'Turkish' suggests a holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkish delight is the gelatinous confectionery, so the answer is a word that can follow Turkish.

clue.text: Duck? Happy sight

parts.note: golden describes happy, prosperous times, as in golden days
the eye is the organ of sight

explanation.surface: Seeing a duck is a welcome sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' might be a cricket score of nil or a verb to dodge; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldeneye is a diving duck with striking golden-yellow eyes, one species of duck.

clue.text: Novel figure noted for wandering?

definitions.meaning: James Joyce's 1922 modernist novel set in Dublin
the Latin name of Odysseus, whose ten-year journey home from Troy is legendary

explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce titled his book after the Roman form of Odysseus, the Greek hero famed for long travels.

clue.text: I regard derisively proposal supporting science

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: SC is an abbreviation of science
an offer is a proposal or bid

explanation.surface: A sceptic sneers at a proposal backing scientific research.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer speaking: the person who mocks.
explanation.definitionFit: One who mocks others derisively, saying 'I regard derisively', is a person who jeers.

clue.text: A key Cyril represented in paint

parts.note: C is a musical key

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist named Cyril is a key figure portrayed in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyril looks like the painter, but 'represented' tells you to rearrange his name, and 'key' is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a quick-drying synthetic paint used by artists; the word names that kind of paint.

clue.text: A regular guide to the stars?

definitions.text: A regular guide to the stars?

parts.words: A regular guide to the stars?
parts.note: an annual publication that charts celestial events, sunrise and tides for the year ahead, issued regularly

explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly book giving astronomical data such as star positions and moon phases.

clue.text: Unproductive director in past

definitions.meaning: yielding little, as in thin or meagre years
David ..., the late British film director of Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.definitionFit: Lean years are poor, unproductive ones, and David Lean was a film director of the past.

clue.text: Blue Guide to city on river

parts.note: the A-Z is the classic British street atlas of a city, especially London
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A blue-covered city guidebook sits by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The A to Z (A-Z) is a well-known British street map book.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright sky-blue colour; a synonym.

clue.text: Morose days possibly to appear — according to them?

definitions.text: Morose days possibly to appear — according to them?

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Gloomy times are forecast, say the pessimists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MOROSE DAYS; the whole clue also describes the answer's prophets of gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomsayers are pessimists predicting disaster, so gloomy days ahead are exactly what they foretell.

clue.text: Classical deity arising in tawdry taste

indicators.note: arising says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ancient god emerges from something in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden run RYTAS, and 'arising' turns it upward, as in a down entry. The draft lacked the 'in' indicator, added here.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a woodland god of Greek mythology, part man and part goat, a minor deity.

clue.text: Decrease resolve

definitions.meaning: read as de-crease, to remove creases from clothes
firmness of will, as in a will of steel

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing removes creases from fabric, and an iron will means strong resolve.

clue.text: Drug that is new probed by book by university academic

indicators.note: something probed has another thing pushed into it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is
prof, short for professor, is an academic

explanation.surface: A new drug is examined by an academic writing a university book.
explanation.walkthrough: BUPROF goes inside IEN, between I and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common anti-inflammatory painkiller, a drug.

clue.text: Leaden feature of newspaper without sign of sparkle

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: an insert is a loose supplement placed inside a newspaper

indicators.note: a sign of a word is its first letter, here from sparkle

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature lacking any sparkle is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S from INSERT gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert and leaden both describe something sluggish, heavy and lifeless; synonyms.

clue.text: Flourishing part of course?

definitions.meaning: thriving and growing healthily, like vigorous young plants
the putting area surrounding each hole on a golf course

explanation.definitionFit: Green growth means flourishing life, and on a golf course each hole has its putting green.

clue.text: Rogue near court — source of stories?

indicators.note: rogue here means acting wildly, so these letters break out of order

explanation.surface: A rogue at the royal court is a fount of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like a noun but signals the rearrangement of NEAR COURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes, someone who supplies stories.
